jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry (Analytical Chemistry)
jobs.description:
Job Description
Assistant Professor of Chemistry (Analytical Chemistry)
The Department of Chemistry at Davidson College invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Analytical Chemistry beginning July 1, 2027. Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Chemistry or a related field before the start of the appointment. Davidson College is committed to access and opportunity for students from all backgrounds and perspectives, and current members of the department actively participate in initiatives that enrich the teaching and mentoring of our students.
The person hired into this position will demonstrate expertise in the development and application of novel analytical methods, particularly within mass spectrometry. Teaching introductory analytical chemistry and instrumental analysis (CHE 220, 320), introductory general chemistry (CHE 115), and advanced electives commensurate with the candidate's training and expertise are in the purview of this position. Contributions to first-year writing courses or lab sciences for students not pursuing STEM are valued. To support a successful research program involving undergraduates, the position includes start-up funds and a personal research lab in a state-of-the-art interdisciplinary science building.
Candidates will be evaluated based on the following application materials (pages are suggested length): a cover letter describing the applicant's interest and qualifications for the position (1-2 pages), a CV (2-5 pages), a teaching statement listing and describing courses/subdisciplines of interest and how the applicant would create a classroom environment that promotes critical thinking and engages all students (2-3 pages), a research statement describing the applicant's proposed research directions if hired into the position including how they would welcome and mentor undergraduates from a variety of backgrounds (3-5 pages), one publication or manuscript representative of the applicant's graduate or postgraduate work, and unofficial undergraduate and graduate academic transcripts. Include in the CV names and contact information for three people from whom letters of recommendation may be solicited by early October. See here for additional information about the area, college, department, position, search process, and specific guidance for materials requested. Preference will be given to applications received by September 18, 2026; the position will remain open until filled. Inquiries may be directed to Mitch Anstey, Chemistry Department Search Committee Chair, mianstey@davidson.edu. Apply Online.
Davidson College is a highly selective, residential, four-year liberal arts college, located 20 miles from Charlotte, NC that is consistently ranked among the top liberal arts colleges in the country.
Davidson places emphasis on excellence in teaching, features outstanding facilities, and provides institutional funding for research, travel, and sabbatical leaves. Davidson faculty and students benefit from small class sizes at all levels. A collegial, respectful atmosphere honors academic achievement and integrity, upholds educational excellence, encourages student-faculty collaborative research, and prioritizes inclusive pedagogy.
About Us
Davidson is a highly selective, nationally ranked, residential liberal arts college located in Davidson, North Carolina, near Charlotte. We seek to hire talented faculty and staff who are committed to achieving excellence within an inclusive community where diverse backgrounds and perspectives are valued.

jobs.title: Histology Professor
jobs.institution: University of Medicine and Health Sciences
jobs.description:
Histology Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor
Basic Science Program
University of Medicine and Health Sciences-St. Kitts
The University of Medicine and Health Sciences-St. Kitts (UMHS) invites applications for a faculty position in Histology at all ranks. UMHS is a state of the art medical school located on the exotic Caribbean Island of St. Kitts. Faculty have a unique opportunity to become involved in the growth and success of the institution, and most importantly the opportunity to educate and nurture a new generation of physicians prepared to meet the 21st century health care delivery in a rapidly changing world.
Responsibilities:
The successful candidate will be responsible for team teaching a course in Histology offered in the first year. The UMHS calendar year has three fifteen week semesters, with two to three weeks break between semesters for faculty leave. Responsibilities include:
Developing and providing students with approved syllabi and learning objectives.
Organizing, preparing, and regularly updating course content.
Delivering effective lectures in the classroom and laboratory utilizing a variety of teaching techniques and state of the art teaching technologies.
Preparing and administering examinations, grading in a timely manner, and providing feedback to students.
Focusing on student success by being available to students during non-teaching time.
Serving on faculty committees.
Supervising students in a variety of activities, including but not limited to, problem based learning activities, human-computer simulation activities in the UMHS virtual hospital ward, and activities in local clinical settings.
Course Description:
Histology 5 credits This course centers on the study of the microscopic structure of normal human cells, tissues, and organs. Virtual microscopy is used to study the structure of basic tissue types and their integration into organs and organ systems. The lectures correlate microscopic and gross anatomy with basic histophysiology and function of organ systems. On completion, the student must be able to identify, describe, and give the function of cells, tissues, structures, and organs of the human body presented via lecture and digital imagery. Students must complete specific performance objectives which accompany individual lecture segments, and, where appropriate, be able to integrate histology with other classes of the curriculum.
Benefits:
US tax free foreign earned income up to ninety thousand dollars a year.
Health Insurance plan, University paid for employee and available to spouse and children at employee's expense
Participation in faculty continuing education or national conferences in the US once annually.
Modern, state of the art campus and facilities in which to teach and conduct research.
Minimum Qualifications:
Must have a passion for teaching
Minimum of an earned Ph.D. in Histology from an accredited graduate school in the U.S., Canada, or the U.K.
Three to five years’ experience teaching Histology in a U.S., Canadian, or U.K. medical program
Proficiency in Microsoft Office including Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English
About UMHS: UMHS offers a traditional four-year Allopathic Doctor of Medicine program leading to the M.D. degree. The university operates year round and offers three semesters per calendar year which start in January, May, and September. Students complete the Basic Science Program at our state of the art campus in St Kitts. The fifth semester occurs at the UMHS campus in Portland, Maine. Students complete their third year of core clinical rotations and fourth year of elective rotations in one of our many affiliated, accredited teaching hospitals throughout the United States. To graduate, students must successfully complete the UMHS medical program and pass the USMLE Step1, Step 2 CK and Step 2 CS. UMHS graduates are eligible to apply for a US or Canadian residency and subsequently may practice medicine in the United States and Canada.
UMHS utilizes innovative teaching techniques such as a 24-bed virtual hospital, small class sizes with individualized attention, and the use of technology to enhance instruction. The faculty is highly credentialed and recruited primarily from the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. UMHS is fully accredited by the St. Kitts/Nevis Accreditation Board as well as the Accreditation Commission on Colleges of Medicine (ACCM). These accreditation standards have been determined by the US Department of Education to be comparable to those of the Liaison Committee on Medical Education which is the accrediting body for US medical schools. Please go on our website and take a video tour of our state of the art campus: (UMHS.ORG/MD)
Send letter of interest, CV, and references to:
Dr. Ed Purcell, epurcell@umhs-sk.net
and hr@umhs-sk.net
See more at: http://www.umhs-sk.org
We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer M/F/D/V

jobs.title: Faculty - Family Medicine (Battle Creek)
jobs.institution: Western Michigan University Homer Stryker M.D. School of Medicine
jobs.description:
Faculty - Family Medicine (Battle Creek)
Western Michigan University Homer Stryker M.D. School of Medicine
Overview:
The Department of Family and Community Medicine (DFCM) at Western Michigan University Homer Stryker M.D. School of Medicine (WMed) continues to lead change for health care in Michigan. The DFCM is seeking an additional, OB-optional faculty member for its 6-6-6 Family Medicine Residency in Battle Creek, MI. Launched in 2019 with tremendous community support, the Battle Creek program partners with both Bronson Battle Creek Hospital and Grace Health, a beautiful Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) that houses the residency’s outpatient practice. This program successfully graduated its first class in 2022 and remains one of the only residencies in the state to be completely based in an FQHC. Known as “Cereal City, USA”, Battle Creek is a vibrant, diverse, well-resourced area with numerous opportunities for collaboration, as the program develops rich learning experiences for trainees while also demonstrating its commitment to improving community health.
This program joins the established WMed Family Medicine Residency in Kalamazoo. The DFCM is currently led by interim co-chairs who emphasize faculty development, education, seed grants, and supported by generous institutional CME and licensing provisions. The two programs work collaboratively to enhance the education of all students and residents, leveraging the unique talents and offerings of each group to strengthen the department. As a community supported residency with the backing of an academic university program we have the best of both worlds. Our residents are trained to competently practice the full scope of family medicine, including outpatient, inpatient, newborn care and obstetrics to serve the community needs of their future practices. The program is open to supporting leading edge skills and innovation in its faculty.
Responsibilities:
Provide clinical services through resident supervision and develop a personal patient panel.
Cover precepting, inpatient, and newborn services; OB is optional.
Recruitment, supervision, education, and assessment of resident physicians.
Participate in quality improvement, utilization review, and outcomes management.
Opportunity to participate and lead in committees and initiatives with our partners.
Provide high-quality instruction for undergraduate and graduate medical education.
Other duties as assigned by the Department.
Qualifications:
MD or DO degree.
Completion of an accredited residency program.
Board certification or eligibility by the American Board of Family Medicine or the American Osteopathic Board of Family Physicians.
Eligibility for Michigan license.
Dedicated commitment to providing a quality educational experience for residents and medical students.
A sense of adventure and willingness to work as a team player as we continue to excel as a new Family Medicine Residency.
About Western Michigan University Homer Stryker M.D. School of Medicine (WMed)
We are committed to excellence and health equity through transformative medical education, high-quality, patient- and family-centered care, innovative research, and community partnerships within a welcoming, supportive, and engaging culture. Our vision is health equity for all in Southwest Michigan through innovation in the practice and study of medicine.
The medical school is a collaboration of Western Michigan University and Kalamazoo's two teaching health systems, Beacon and Bronson Healthcare. The medical school is a private nonprofit corporation supported by private gifts, clinical revenues, research activities, tuition, and endowment income. WMed is the recipient of a $100 million foundational gift and the Empowering Futures Gift, a philanthropic commitment of $300 million to support the mission of the medical school. WMed contributes to the economic vitality of Southwest Michigan through the services we provide, as well as the creation of 1,600 new jobs, with an estimated annual economic impact of $353 million in Kalamazoo and Calhoun counties.
WMed is fully accredited by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education and the Higher Learning Commission. The medical school offers a comprehensive, innovative four-year Doctor of Medicine degree program as well as a Master of Science degree program in Biomedical Sciences. We train physicians in 10 residencies and four fellowships accredited by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education. To support our educational mission, we have Joint Accreditation for interprofessional continuing education, which incorporates accreditation by the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education.
WMed Health is the clinical practice of the medical school with more than 300 providers offering comprehensive primary care and specialty services in several locations throughout the Kalamazoo and Battle Creek areas. Faculty in the Department of Pathology serve as the Office of the Medical Examiner for counties throughout Michigan and northern Indiana.
The W.E. Upjohn M.D. Campus located in downtown Kalamazoo serves as the primary educational facility with student study and social spaces, team-based learning halls, faculty and administrative offices, a state-of-the-art Simulation Center accredited by the Society for Simulation in Healthcare, basic science research labs, as well as toxicology and forensic pathology labs.
WMed builds upon Kalamazoo’s century-long foundation of drug discovery and medical device development with a strategic investment in clinical, laboratory, community, and educational research. The Center for Immunobiology, Center for Clinical Research, Research Histology Lab, Innovation Center, and Human Research Protection Program contribute to the medical school’s advancement of knowledge through innovation and discovery.
Equal Employment Opportunity Employer in compliance with applicable State and Federal law.
Questions and inquiries can be directed to Dr. Michael Busha, Professor and Co-Chair, Department of Family & Community Medicine at mike.busha@wmed.edu or Dr. Lauren Piper, Vice President of Clinical Affairs and Co-Chair, lauren.piper@wmed.edu; qualified applicants should apply online at www.wmed.edu (click on employment) or directly here.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Media Studies
jobs.institution: University of North Carolina at Greensboro, Department of Media Studies
jobs.description:
University Information
Located in North Carolina’s third largest city, UNC Greensboro is among the most diverse, learner-centered public research universities in the state, with 18,000 students in eight colleges and schools pursuing more than 150 areas of undergraduate and over 200 areas of graduate study. UNCG continues to be recognized nationally for academic excellence, access, and affordability. UNCG is ranked No. 1 most affordable institution in North Carolina for net cost by the N.Y. Times and No. 1 in North Carolina for social mobility by The Wall Street Journal — helping first-generation and lower-income students find paths to prosperity. Designated an Innovation and Economic Prosperity University by the Association of Public and Land-grant Universities, UNCG is a community-engaged research institution with a portfolio of more than $67M in research and creative activity. The University’s 2,600 staff help create an annual economic impact for the Piedmont Triad region in excess of $1B.
Primary Purpose of the Organizational Unit
The Department of Media Studies in the College of Arts and Sciences focuses on the creative production and critical analyses of a range of moving-image media. The faculty is composed of award-winning artists, scholars, and practitioners. The Department is housed in the Brown Building and in the Carmichael Center. Originally constructed to serve the University of North Carolina public broadcasting system, the Carmichael Center now holds the Department’s soundstage, screening room, production classrooms, editing lab, audio recording studio, and location production equipment inventory. The Department enhances the curriculum with opportunities to learn outside of the traditional classroom setting and participate in a variety of media productions. These include the Department’s internship program, registered student organizations for film production, and its client-based production clinic, Spartan Media Productions.
Position Summary
The Department of Media Studies at UNC Greensboro invites applications for a Tenure-Track Assistant Professor of Media Studies with an emphasis on the History and Critical Analysis of Interactive and Emerging Media to begin August 1, 2027. We seek a scholar whose research explores the history, theory, and cultural and societal impacts of digital platforms, interactive, and emerging media. The successful candidate will have an established record of scholarship in emerging media research, with expertise in areas such as Cinematic AI, VR/AR/XR, internet subcultures, video games, interactive and immersive media, or virtual production. Candidates should be prepared to teach undergraduate and graduate courses in media theory and studies, including History of Digital Media, Media Theory, Seminar in Media Studies, and Theory and History of Emerging Media. Responsibilities include ongoing scholarly and professional activity, and service to the department, college, and university.
Required Qualifications:
Candidates must hold or anticipate a Ph.D. in Media Studies or a related discipline by August 1, 2027.
Evidence of a clear, ongoing scholarly research agenda.
College teaching experience.
Deep knowledge of critical-historical methods applied to emerging media.
Commitment to the collaborative process within our department, as well as with other UNCG academic programs and/or the community.
We are especially interested in candidates with experience helping first-generation, diverse, and/or non-traditional student populations find their creative voice and managing experiential “field” learning.
Instructions to Applicants
All materials must be submitted electronically through the online application process. Required application materials include:
Letter of Application
Current Curriculum Vitae
Scholarship Statement
Teaching Statement: Record of teaching excellence, including teaching philosophy, evaluations if available, and sample syllabi (with syllabi emphasis on emerging media)
Names, email addresses, and phone numbers of 3 professional references
Only complete applications will be considered. Review of applications will begin on October 1st, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.
For additional information or to apply for this position (# 1667), please visit our website at https://spartantalent.uncg.edu/

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Salary

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Instruction in Musicology
jobs.description:
The Bienen School of Music at Northwestern University invites applications for two full-time faculty appointments in Musicology beginning September 1, 2027. Rank and salary will be commensurate with experience and accomplishment. These positions are not tenure eligible.
The Bienen School offers highly selective, conservatory-level training within a top-ranked research university and features a dedicated faculty, unparalleled facilities, and proximity to the vibrant music community of Chicago.
Responsibilities
Responsibilities include teaching in the undergraduate musicology core curriculum and graduate history review, along with electives courses and graduate seminars in the candidates’ areas of expertise. These professors will also share the coordination of the school’s nonmajor general music curriculum. This includes pedagogical guidance and support for PhD and DMA student instructors and coordination of summer session course offerings. The teaching load will be 5–6 courses per year split over 3 academic quarters, depending upon administrative responsibilities.
Bienen musicology faculty are expected to work collaboratively with colleagues in supervising undergraduate and graduate research projects, participating on dissertation committees, advising undergraduate students, and implementing creative curricular development. The musicology program is housed within the Department of Music Studies and as such, collaboration extends to the department’s other three programs (Music Composition, Music Education, and Music Theory and Cognition), as well as the Department of Music Performance.
Required Qualifications
Applicants must have a PhD in musicology/ethnomusicology. Preference will be given to candidates who demonstrate outstanding pedagogical achievement and have intellectual interests in topics that complement the strengths of the school’s current faculty. We are especially interested in candidates with expertise in Western art music after 1800, popular music, jazz, and the study of music and technology.
Contract length and Reappointment
Candidates hired at the rank of Assistant Professor of Instruction will be given an initial one-year appointment. Upon completion of successful review, they will receive 3-year appointments with the possibility of renewal depending upon curricular need and budgetary conditions. Candidates hired at the rank of Associate Professor of Instruction will receive a 3-year appointment with the possibility of renewal depending upon curricular need and budgetary conditions. Promotion is possible to ranks of Associate or Full Professor of Instruction.
Salary
The expected base pay based on rank is as follows:
Assistant Professor of Instruction: $67,500-$80,000
Associate Professor of Instruction: $81,000-$92,500
Northwestern University has provided a pay range representing its good faith estimate of what the university reasonably expects to pay for the position. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate; years since terminal degree, training, and field or discipline; departmental budget availability; internal equity; and external market pay for comparable jobs.
Benefits
At Northwestern, we are proud to provide meaningful and competitive beneﬁts. The available beneﬁts package for this position will include health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance; paid medical/sick and parental leave; tuition beneﬁts for the employee and dependents; pre-tax and ﬂex spending accounts for commuting and dependent care; generous retirement savings options; and wellness programs. For a comprehensive overview of available beneﬁts, including eligibility details, visit us at
https://www.northwestern.edu/hr/beneﬁts/index.html to learn more.
Application
Screening begins November 16, 2026, and continues until the positions are filled. Candidates should submit:
• Letter of application
• Curriculum vitae
• Statement of teaching philosophy and methods
• Two course syllabi
• Names and contact information for three references.
Apply online at: https://facultyrecruiting.northwestern.edu/apply/MjYxNA== or access the application process via the Bienen School's website at: https://music.northwestern.edu/careers.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Organizational Behavior
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Leeds School of Business at the University of Colorado
Boulder is hiring an Assistant/Associate Professor of
Organizational Behavior position in Organizational Leadership and
Information Analytics (OLIA) Division, starting in Fall 2027.
We are seeking candidates with recent success or a strong potential
in publishing high-quality and impactful research in leading
management journals. A successful candidate should exhibit a strong
willingness and ability to teach courses in organizational behavior
and management, as well as a strong willingness and ability to
effectively interact with faculty colleagues, students, staff, and
external constituents. We are interested in candidates with a
grounding in Organizational Behavior or an allied discipline who
are pursuing work in the area of Organizational Behavior.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
The University of Colorado Boulder, and the city of Boulder, offer
a rich intellectual, cultural, recreational, and family-friendly
environment. The economy of the Front Range of Colorado is strong,
and private support for the University and the Leeds School is
increasing steadily, as evidenced by our new programs and solid MBA
program.
The University of Colorado and the Leeds School of Business are
nationally recognized for the excellence of our faculty, programs,
and students. By joining Leeds, you will become part of a collegial
and productive group of Organizational Behavior scholars committed
to research and teaching excellence. Our faculty actively publish
and serve on the editorial boards of leading management journals,
including but not limited to the Academy of Management Journal,
Academy of Management Review, Organization Science, Journal of
Applied Psychology, and Organizational Behavior and Human Decision
Processes. Our faculty are also passionate about conducting
research that has a meaningful societal or practical impact.
Boulder is a satellite community of about 107,000 people with
excellent schools located 30 minutes from downtown Denver, a few
hours from world-renown ski resorts, at the heart of the Colorado
startup ecosystem, and has over 300 sunny days each year. The
Boulder/Denver area is one of the fastest growing regions in
America, has a metropolitan population of about 3.4 million, and is
surrounded by stunning scenery. The University of Colorado also
offers an excellent early childhood and preschool education
facility attended by students who collectively speak over 50
languages.
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Minimum qualifications include a doctorate in Organizational
Behavior or an allied discipline (e.g., Human Resources,
Psychology, Labor and Employment Relations / Industrial Relations),
a strong willingness and ability to teach courses in organizational
behavior and management, and the demonstrated ability to conduct
high-quality and impactful (quantitative and/or qualitative)
academic research. Candidates who are Ph.D. students must be close
to completion of their Ph.D. degrees (all completed but Ph.D.
dissertation). The Ph.D. degree should be obtained before the
appointment starts.
What We Can Offer
The salary range for an Assistant Professor ($190,000–$200,000) or
Associate Professor ($215,000–$230,000). Additional benefits
include allowance with relocation expenses and for a computer, FDA
(Faculty Development Account), and a specific amount of guaranteed
summer research support.
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. Explore additional perks and programs through
the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be creative. Be impactful. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. degree or equivalent in Organizational
Behavior or a closely related field or be close to completion of a
Ph.D. degree (all completed but Ph.D. dissertation). The Ph.D.
degree should be obtained before the appointment starts. We are
seeking candidates with recent success or strong potential in
publishing high-quality and impactful (quantitative and/or
qualitative) research in leading management journals. A successful
candidate should exhibit a strong willingness and ability to teach
courses in organizational behavior and management, as well as a
strong willingness and ability to effectively interact with faculty
colleagues, students, staff, and external constituents. We are
interested in candidates with a grounding in Organizational
Behavior or an allied discipline who are pursuing work in the area
of Organizational Behavior.
Note: Candidates who have not yet conferred their degree will be
appointed as an Instructor until the semester following the degree
conferral.
What We Would Like You to Have
Desired qualifications include an established program of research
published in leading management journals, or a demonstrated
potential in building a strong research pipeline for publications
in leading management journals, as well as at least 1 year of
experience of teaching organizational behavior and management at
the undergraduate, master’s, and/or doctoral levels. Teaching
experience can be gained during a candidate’s graduate studies.
Teaching duties could include undergraduate/master’s students and
doctoral students.
Special Instructions
To apply, please submit the following materials:
Resume/CV
Cover Letter
Research Statement
Teaching Statement
Evidence of research effectiveness (e.g., 1–3 journal
publications, conference papers, and/or working papers combined
into one PDF; If any, at least one submission should be
first-authored)
Evidence of teaching effectiveness (e.g., student evaluations,
course syllabi, and teaching portfolios combined into one PDF)
During the application process you will need to enter contact
information for three references. We will request letters of
recommendation and additional materials, if needed, as the search
progresses.
Applications received by September 28, 2026 will receive
full consideration. Position will remain open until filled.
Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For
consideration, applications must be submitted through CU Boulder Jobs.
In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, in
any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying
information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school
attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting
or removing this information.
Posting Contact Information
Posting Contact Name: Boulder Campus Human Resources
Posting Contact Email: Recruiting@colorado.edu

jobs.description:

position
Assistant Teaching Professor, Sports Nutrition
Department of Human Physiology and Nutrition
Helen and Arthur E. Johnson Beth-El College of Nursing and
Health Sciences
Elevate Your Career at UCCS: Innovate, Inspire, and Impact in
the Rockies!
Who We Are
The University of Colorado Colorado Springs
(UCCS) is a premier educational institution that prides itself on

n our team! UCCS is committed to academic excellence, professional

At the base of the Rocky Mountains, Colorado Springs is captivated by its

Salary R ange : $ 25,000 - $27,500 per

Summary

labs); mentor undergraduate and graduate students in and outside of

demonstrate collaborative interests and collegiality in all aspects
of university and community engagement. Candidates with expertise
in the areas of nutrition, exercise science and other affiliated
fields are encouraged to apply. Applicants should possess good

Essential Functions
The duties and responsibilities of the position include, but are
not limited to:
Teaching & Instruction (80%)
Develop and deliver high-quality undergraduate and/or
graduate courses in the assigned discipline, using evidence-based
teaching practices to promote student learning and
engagement.
Design course syllabi, assignments, and assessments aligned
with program learning outcomes and accreditation
standards.
Facilitate classroom, laboratory, and/or online instruction
using appropriate pedagogical strategies and technology
tools.
Provide timely and constructive feedback on student work to
support academic success.
Maintain regular office hours and academic advising for

Integrate experiential learning opportunities (e.g.,

Mentor graduate students in capstone projects in nutrition

Continuously update course content to reflect current

Examples of courses that may be taught: HPNU 1050: Personal

6900: Nutrition Seminar.
Serv ice (20%)

Engage in student recruitment and retention activities,

Collaborate with colleagues on program assessment and

improvement.
Contribute to community and professional service through
partnerships, guest lectures, or involvement in relevant

Mentor adjunct faculty or graduate teaching assistants to

Assist in organizing departmental events, seminars, and

This role emphasizes instructional excellence and student
success, requiring independent judgment in curriculum design and
classroom management.
Decision-making involves selecting appropriate teaching

Tentative Search Timeline

2026.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all

apply, including protected veterans and individuals with

In accordance with the Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, UCCS does not
discriminate based on sex in our employment or compensation
practices.
Qualifications :
A Master's Degree in nutrition, human physiology, exercise
science or closely related field is mandatory.
Registered Dietitian/Nutritionist (RD/RDN) is
preferred.
International Olympic Committee Diploma in Sports Nutrition
or Certified Specialist in Sports Dietetics (CSSD) is

1 or more academic terms of teaching experience is
preferred.
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to
perform each of the established essential functions and meet the

requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill,
ability, physical and environmental conditions required of the

Applicants with disabilities: If you have a mental or physical

The University of Colorado Colorado Springs has implemented a

jobs.title: Associate Vice Chancellor for Faculty Affairs and Faculty Success
jobs.description:
Position Details
University of Colorado | Denver
Official Title: Associate Vice Chancellor
Working Title: Associate Vice Chancellor for Faculty Affairs and
Faculty Success
FTE: Full-time
Salary Range: $200,000 to $220,000
Position #00350743 – Requisition #40962
***Open to CU Denver employees only***
About the University of Colorado Denver
Millions of moments start at CU Denver, a place where innovation,
research, and learning meet in the heart of a global city. We're
the state's premier public urban research university with more than
100 in-demand, top-ranked bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degree
programs. We partner with diverse learners—at any stage of their
life and career—for transformative educational experiences. Across
seven schools and colleges, our leading faculty inspires and works
alongside students to solve complex challenges and produce
impactful creative work. As part of the state's largest university
system, CU Denver is a major contributor to the Colorado economy,
with 2,000 employees and an annual economic impact of $665 million.
To learn more about how CU Denver helps learners meet their moment,
visit ucdenver.edu.
Job Description
* Applications are accepted electronically ONLY at
www.cu.edu/cu-careers *
The Associate Vice Chancellor for Faculty Affairs and Professional
Development (AVCFAPD) is a senior academic leader and a member of
the Provost's Leadership Team, reporting directly to the Provost
and Executive Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs. The AVCFAPD
provides strategic leadership for faculty affairs, faculty success,
and academic culture across the CU Denver campus.
This role is responsible for advancing faculty excellence and
wellbeing across the full faculty lifecycle, including recruitment,
onboarding, development, evaluation, advancement, governance, and
transition. Central to the position is fostering an inclusive,
supportive, and high-performing academic environment in which
faculty thrive as teachers, scholars, mentors, and institutional
leaders.
In alignment with CU Denver's mission as a public, urban serving,
equity focused research university, the AVCFAPD leads and
coordinates institutional policies, practices, and initiatives that
support faculty success; promote excellence and innovation in
teaching and pedagogy; ensure fair and consistent faculty personnel
processes; and align faculty work with student success and
institutional priorities.
What you will do:
Faculty Affairs and Academic Personnel Strategy
Provide institutional leadership for faculty affairs and
academic personnel strategy across the faculty lifecycle, ensuring
that policies and practices advance academic excellence,
institutional priorities, and a strong and sustainable
faculty.
Provide university-wide leadership and oversight for faculty
recruitment, appointment, onboarding, evaluation, promotion and
tenure, post-tenure review, sabbaticals and leaves, grievances,
retention, and separation.
Lead institutional faculty hiring planning in partnership with
the Provost and deans, aligning faculty investments with academic
priorities, enrollment and program needs, research strengths, and
available resources.
Establish and interpret university-level faculty policies and
standards and ensure consistent, equitable, and effective
implementation across schools and colleges.
Ensure institutional compliance with faculty credentialing,
accreditation, Regent and System requirements, and applicable state
and federal requirements.
Advise the Provost, deans, and other academic leaders on
complex faculty personnel matters and emerging issues affecting the
faculty.
Faculty Development, Teaching Excellence, and Academic
Leadership
Provide strategic leadership for faculty development across
career stages, advancing faculty effectiveness as teachers,
scholars, mentors, institutional citizens, and academic
leaders.
Lead university-wide strategy for teaching excellence and
pedagogical innovation, including effective use of emerging
technologies and evolving instructional modalities.
Advance faculty practices that strengthen student learning,
engagement, belonging, and success across CU Denver's diverse
student population.
Develop a robust faculty leadership pipeline through leadership
development, mentoring, and preparation for roles including program
director, department chair/head, associate dean, and other academic
leadership positions.
Partner with deans and academic leaders to strengthen the
onboarding, development, effectiveness, and success of department
chairs and other faculty leaders.
Foster mentoring, professional growth, and career advancement
opportunities responsive to faculty across appointment types,
disciplines, career stages, and roles.
Faculty Performance, Workload, Recognition, and Retention
Provide institutional leadership for faculty performance
management, including annual evaluation, workload, professional
development leave, sabbaticals, and related policies and
processes.
Establish and interpret university-level expectations and
frameworks for faculty workload and differentiated contributions,
working with academic leaders to promote appropriate consistency,
transparency, and accountability across units.
Use institutional data and evidence to identify faculty
workforce trends, workload patterns, compensation and retention
issues, and opportunities to strengthen faculty effectiveness and
sustainability.
Lead institutional strategies for faculty recognition,
retention, and career advancement, including university-level
awards and recognition of excellence in teaching, research and
creative work, mentorship, service, and public impact.
Partner with deans, Human Resources, and other university
leaders on faculty compensation, salary equity, retention, and
related workforce strategies.
Shared Governance, Faculty Culture, and Institutional Change
Serve as a principal liaison between the Provost's Office and
faculty governance, fostering effective shared governance and
constructive engagement among faculty, academic leaders, and
university administration.
Advise the Provost and senior academic leadership on faculty
perspectives, emerging concerns, and issues affecting academic
culture and institutional effectiveness.
Lead and support institutional change initiatives affecting
faculty roles, policies, expectations, and academic culture.
Foster a high-performing academic culture that values
excellence in teaching, research and creative work, mentorship,
service, collaboration, and shared responsibility for the
university's mission.
Facilitate constructive engagement on complex or sensitive
faculty and academic issues and strengthen institutional capacity
for productive dialogue and change.
Faculty Success, Equity, and Well-Being
Provide institutional leadership for strategies that promote
faculty success, professional sustainability, well-being, equity,
and belonging.
Advance equitable and transparent practices in faculty
recruitment, appointment, compensation, evaluation, workload,
mentoring, advancement, leadership development, and
recognition.
Ensure institutional compliance with applicable faculty
employment and compensation requirements in partnership with Human
Resources, University Counsel, deans, and CU System offices.
Identify systemic barriers to faculty success and work with
academic leaders to develop institutional strategies that
strengthen faculty experience, engagement, retention, and
effectiveness.
Qualifications you already possess (Minimum
Qualifications)
Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of
hire.
• Earned doctorate from an accredited institution.
• A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible leadership
experience in higher education, with significant responsibility for
faculty affairs, academic administration, or faculty
development.
• Demonstrated expertise in faculty personnel policies, evaluation
processes, and shared governance.
• Documented experience leading faculty professional development,
mentoring, or institutional initiatives.
Preferred Qualification to possess (Preferred
Qualifications)
• Record of accomplishment at the rank of full professor or
equivalent.
• Experience leading an academic unit at or above the level of
department chair/head.
• Demonstrated leadership in teaching excellence, faculty pedagogy,
or academic innovation.
• Experience at a public research university and/or equity serving
institution.
• Experience navigating multicampus or system level governance
environments.
• Demonstrated success managing organizational change and conflict
in complex academic settings.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
• Deep understanding of academic culture and faculty roles.
• Ability to lead through influence, collaboration, and
evidence-based decision making.
• Strong analytical and organizational skills with the ability to
manage multiple priorities.
• Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and
belonging.
• Ability to effectively partner with senior leadership, faculty
governance, and campus stakeholders.
• Knowledge of faculty HR practices, including recruitment,
evaluation, compensation, and workload analysis.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication
skills.
Conditions of Employment
• Occasional work during the evening and/or weekends may be
required.
• This position follows a hybrid work structure where employees can
work remotely or from the office, as needed, based on demands of
specific tasks or personal work preferences. Working from the
office is encouraged when working on tasks that require a high
degree of collaboration.

27-07 Tenure-Track Assistant Professor of Biochemistry
Position Summary
Join a vibrant equity-minded campus whose excellence is reflected in its community, cultural engagement, and student success. The Department of Chemistry invites applicants for a Full-time, 9-month, Tenure-Track, Assistant Professor of Biochemistry position. The position begins in August 2027.
West Chester University (WCU), a member of the Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education, is a public, comprehensive institution committed to offering high-quality undergraduate education, selected post-baccalaureate and graduate programs, and a variety of educational and cultural resources for its students, alumni, and citizens of southeastern Pennsylvania. The University offers more than 100 graduate and undergraduate programs in the sciences and mathematics, business and public management, arts and humanities, health sciences, education and social work, music, and interdisciplinary studies. We are a community of educators dedicated to developing graduates who succeed personally and professionally and contribute to the common good.
The mission of the Department of Chemistry, part of the College of the Sciences and Mathematics, is committed to excellence in teaching, scholarship, and student success. The Department offers bachelor’s degrees in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmaceutical Product Development (PPD), Forensic and Toxicological Chemistry (accredited by FEPAC), and Chemistry–Biology. The Chemistry and Biochemistry degree programs are certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS), and the Chemistry–Biology program is accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB), ensuring that students receive a high-quality education aligned with nationally recognized standards. Learn more about the Department of Chemistry.
The faculty member will teach undergraduate level courses that may be offered via in-person, online, and/or hybrid instructional modality formats depending on departmental needs. The ideal candidate will demonstrate excellence in teaching through evidence-based and innovative instructional practices that promote student engagement and success. The person embraces experiential learning through hands-on laboratory, research, and other high-impact educational experiences. The faculty member will collaborate with colleagues to support student success and contribute to the department's teaching, research, and service mission.
Responsibilities include:
Teach undergraduate lecture in Biochemistry, General Chemistry as well as other laboratory courses in the Chemistry curriculum via approved modalities Additional courses may be assigned based in area(s) of specialization depending on departmental needs
Develop and maintain an active research program in biochemistry or a closely related field that engages undergraduate students
Collaborate with faculty to support curriculum development, experiential learning opportunities, and student success
Advise and mentor undergraduate students, providing academic, research, and professional development support
Serve the Department and University community through participation in various committees and outreach activities
Perform other duties as assigned

Ph.D. in Biochemistry or a closely related field. ABD may be considered – Doctoral dissertation must be successfully completed on or before July 31, 2027

Experience working in or conducting research in biochemistry or a closely related field
Experience advising, mentoring, or supervising undergraduate and/or graduate students

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Political Science, Tenure-Track, Fall 2027
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The Department of Political Science in Wilkinson College of Arts,
Humanities, and Social Sciences at Chapman University invites
applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Political
Science with a primary focus on American politics. Successful
candidates will also demonstrate the ability to teach courses on
research methods. Employment will begin in August 2027.
Chapman University is a nationally-ranked, R2 Carnegie Classified,
private institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate
programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern
California’s most diverse and vibrant regions. Chapman’s campuses
are home to nearly 10,000 students representing 50 states, three
territories, and 87 countries. The 11 schools and colleges of
Chapman offer 65 bachelor's, 53 master's, and six doctoral
programs, along with nearly 60 minors and 17 accelerated and bridge
programs. Classes are taught by the more than 1,100 dedicated
faculty members who are leaders in their fields, including Nobel
Prize recipients, MacArthur Fellows, National Medal of Science
honorees, former U.S. Supreme Court clerks, and Emmy, Grammy, and
Academy Award winners.
The Department of Political Science is committed to educating
students to become effective democratic citizens, both locally and
globally. We provide a distinctive, challenging, and personalized
learning environment anchored in critical thinking and student
research. Through a variety of courses, internships, and other
experiential learning opportunities, students gain a theoretical
and practical knowledge of politics. Students who graduate with a
degree in Political Science will be well-equipped for graduate
studies or careers in law, government, public policy, government
relations, or the nonprofit sector.
The mission of Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social
Sciences is to foster rigorous inquiry among students through a
curriculum grounded in the liberal arts that is scholarly,
creative, interdisciplinary, and experiential. The College plays an
important and unique role in the educational journey of every
Chapman student and aims to ensure that graduates are prepared to
assume their responsibility as global citizens, acting
knowledgeably and providing compassionate leadership in our
community and world. More information about Wilkinson College is
available at www.chapman.edu/wilkinson
.
Responsibilities
Plan, develop, and deliver high-quality courses in American
politics, as well as in research methods.
Maintain an active research agenda in the field of American
politics that results in impactful scholarly contributions to the
field.
Actively participate in departmental, college, and university
service.
Qualifications
Required
A Ph.D. in Political Science or related field from an
accredited institution of higher education by August 2027.
In-depth knowledge and expertise in the subject area or
discipline related to the courses they will be teaching.
Record of impactful scholarly publication and/or clear and
strong potential for sustained and impactful research
productivity.
Preferred
Experience teaching courses in American politics and/or
research methods
Evidence of excellence in teaching and a student-centered
approach to teaching, including the ability to provide support and
guidance to students
Experience collaborating with colleagues, department chairs,
and academic administrators on curriculum development and
institutional initiatives
Application Instructions
Qualified candidates are invited to submit the following
electronically:
Cover Letter
Curriculum Vitae
Research Statement (2 pages max)
Teaching Statement (2 pages max)
Three confidential letters of reference
Inquiries can be directed to the Search Committee Chair, Dr. John
Compton (compton@chapman.edu), and should use ‘American Politics
Search’ as the email subject line.
Application reviews will begin immediately and will continue until
the position is filled. Salary is competitive and will be
commensurate with experience. The salary range for this position is
$90,000 to $107,000. This position is contingent on final budget
approval. Successful completion of a background check is required
for the final candidate.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Chapman University is an equal opportunity employer that provides
equal employment opportunities to all individuals, regardless of
their protected characteristics. All qualified applicants and
employees are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration
for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex,
sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national
origin, ancestry, citizenship status, physical disability, mental
disability, medical condition, military and veteran status, marital
status, pregnancy, genetic information or any other characteristic
protected by state or federal law.

Position Overview
Primary Purpose of Position
The Department of Psychology, within the Hairston College of Health
and Human Sciences at North Carolina Agricultural and Technical
State University, is seeking an assistant or associate professor
with a Ph.D. in Clinical Psychology . Preference
will be given to candidates with a research focus in 1) substance
use disorders, 2) memory and cognition, 3) applied psychology, or
4) health psychology. The selected candidate will be expected to
provide student-centered instruction in undergraduate courses in
their discipline. They will also teach graduate-level courses for
the MS in Health Psychology and the PhD in Applied Psychology in
courses aligned with their area of expertise.
Faculty in this role are expected to contribute to student
advising, mentoring, curriculum development, and engage in program
assessment. The ideal candidate will be expected to: (i) establish
and sustain a strong, externally-funded research program aligned
with their field of expertise; (ii) produce an excellent record of
scholarly publications; (iii) incorporate modern pedagogical skills
in undergraduate and graduate psychology courses; (iv) supervise
and support psychology students in independent research projects;
and (v) engage in service at the department, college and university
as well as to appropriate community and professional
organizations.
This is a 9-month, tenure-track position.
Primary Function of Organizational Unit
North Carolina A & T State University is a public land grant
high research institution that is committed to teaching and
learning, scholarly and creative research, and effective engagement
and public service. As the largest HBCU in the nation, our
enrollment is over 15,000 students, and our workforce includes over
2,000 employees. North Carolina A&T State University offers
over 90-degree programs at the bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral
levels through eight academic colleges. The University is one of
the sixteen constituent units of the University of North Carolina (
UNC ) and is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and
Schools ( SACS ). The strategic vision, preeminence 2030, focuses
the University on interdisciplinary scholarly activities in a
learner-centered environment.
The John R. and Kathy R. Hairston College of Health and Human
Sciences ( HCHHS ) is comprised of six departments and the School
of Nursing. The HCHHS offers the following undergraduate degree
programs; Communication Sciences and Disorders, Health Services
Management, Kinesiology, Nursing, Psychology, Social Work, and
Sociology. At the graduate level, HCHHS offers four graduate degree
programs including the Masters in Physician Assistant Studies (
MSPA ), Master of Social Work ( MSW ), Master of Science in Health
Psychology and Ph.D. in Social Work, PhD in Applied Psychology, and
Doctor of Nursing Practice ( DNP ). The HCHHS is also home to the
Center of Excellence in Integrative Health Disparities and Equity
Research ( CIHDER ), which serves as a multidisciplinary hub for
research and community engagement aimed at advancing health for
all. The HCHHS capitalizes on the synergistic relationships between
these departments to develop advanced academic programming, enhance
the mentoring of trainees, and conduct collaborative
multidisciplinary research and scholastic activity.
The Department of Psychology is a supportive community of committed
faculty and practitioners whose goals are to introduce students to
the ideas and concepts relevant to this discipline, encourage
interdisciplinary learning, prepare students for study in graduate
school, prepare students for entry-level jobs requiring knowledge
in psychology, and train students to conduct both basic and applied
research. These goals are achieved through quality classroom
instruction, departmental colloquia, departmental student
organizations, internship opportunities through independent study,
and individualized research projects. The Department of Psychology
has 980 enrolled undergraduate students and 45 graduate students.
The department is seeking candidates to join a growing program with
a highly interactive and productive faculty.

jobs.title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor, Finance
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Finance at Loyola Marymount University (LMU), a Carnegie-classified R2 institution in the mainstream of American Catholic higher education, seeks outstanding applicants for the position of Assistant Professor of Finance (Tenure-Track) who value its Mission and share its commitment to inclusive excellence and the building of a just society.
Who We Are
LMU is federally recognized as a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI) and is recognized by the State of California as a Black-Serving Institution (BSI). These designations reflect the university’s continuing commitment to supporting student success, belonging, and thriving within a diverse academic community.
As a Catholic, Jesuit, and Marymount University, LMU seeks faculty members who will contribute to the university’s mission to encourage learning, educate the whole person, and serve faith and promote justice. Faculty are encouraged to contribute to the LMU Core Curriculum, such as through the development of a First-Year Seminar and/or courses incorporating Engaged Learning for Mission. We welcome candidates who demonstrate both disciplinary excellence and a clear capacity to advance LMU’s mission through their teaching, scholarly, creative, professional, and service-related contributions, as appropriate to their discipline and appointment.
LMU’s faculty play a central role in realizing our mission by shaping learning environments, advancing knowledge, mentoring and forming students, and contributing to the intellectual and institutional life of the university. The successful candidate will engage students as whole persons and pursue scholarly and creative work that promotes justice, equity, and the common good in alignment with LMU’s teacher-scholar model, contributing to the larger body of knowledge while setting an example for the importance of lifelong learning. A teacher-scholar at LMU is dedicated to 1) teaching a diverse student body in a transformative learning environment, 2) developing a thriving portfolio in research/scholarship/creative works and mentoring students, 3) participating in service activities at the academic, professional, and/or community levels, and 4) working towards greater equity, inclusion, belonging, and accessibility for all in the profession. For more information about our current faculty, please visit Join Our Faculty.
Appointment Type and Details
This is a tenure-track faculty appointment. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Finance or a closely related field, conferred no later than the position start date of August 15, 2027. This full-time, 9-month academic appointment (August – May) has an annual salary paid over 12 consecutive months, allowing for continuous benefits coverage. The standard teaching load for tenure-track faculty is 2-2-2-3 over a two-year cycle, with expectations to advise students and provide service to the department, college, and university. For the first two years, the teaching load is reduced to 2-2-2-2.
Position Description and Department Environment
The Department of Finance seeks a teacher-scholar with research and teaching interests in all areas of finance. The ideal candidate will demonstrate interest and potential to engage in collaborative, interdisciplinary research and teaching. Faculty responsibilities include maintaining an active program of scholarship, teaching (typical class size ranges from 20 to 30 students), advising undergraduate and/or graduate students, mentoring students, and contributing to department, college, and university service.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Our Invitation
The Department of Theological Studies at Loyola Marymount University (LMU), a Carnegie classified R2 institution in the mainstream of American Catholic higher education, seeks outstanding applicants for the tenure-track Assistant Professor of Christianity in Late Antiquity position who value its Mission and share its commitment to inclusive excellence and the building of a just society.
Who We Are
LMU is federally recognized as a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI) and is recognized by the State of California as a Black-Serving Institution (BSI). These designations reflect the university’s continuing commitment to supporting student success, belonging, and thriving within a diverse academic community.
As a Catholic, Jesuit, and Marymount university, LMU seeks faculty members who will contribute to the university’s mission to encourage learning, educate the whole person, and serve faith and promote justice. Faculty are encouraged to contribute to the LMU Core Curriculum, such as through the development of a First-Year Seminar and/or courses incorporating Engaged Learning for Mission. We welcome candidates who demonstrate both disciplinary excellence and a clear capacity to advance LMU’s mission through their teaching, scholarly, creative, professional, and service-related contributions, as appropriate to their discipline and appointment.
LMU’s faculty play a central role in realizing our mission by shaping learning environments, advancing knowledge, mentoring and forming students, and contributing to the intellectual and institutional life of the university. The successful candidate will engage students as whole persons and pursue scholarly and creative work that promotes justice, equity, and the common good in alignment with LMU’s teacher-scholar model, contributing to the larger body of knowledge while setting an example for the importance of lifelong learning. A teacher-scholar at LMU is dedicated to 1) teaching a diverse student body in a transformative learning environment, 2) developing a thriving portfolio in research/scholarship/creative works and mentoring students, 3) participating in service activities at the academic, professional, and/or community levels, and 4) working towards greater equity, inclusion, belonging, and accessibility for all in the profession. For more information about our current faculty, please visit Join Our Faculty.
Position Description
The Assistant Professor will be dedicated to the scholarship and teaching of the first millennium of Christianity, from its post-apostolic period (ca. 100 CE) down to the later Byzantine or early Medieval period (ca. 1000 CE). The ideal candidate’s training and research agenda should reflect the regional and linguistic diversity of the “Christianities” which existed in Late Antiquity: from Egypt, Palestine, Syria, and Lebanon in the East to Africa, Gaul, Italy, and Spain in the West, and beyond. In addition to church fathers, the ideal candidate’s teaching will also bring attention to neglected church mothers. Furthermore, the ideal candidate will be prepared to teach not only the major figures within Christian orthodoxy but also more marginalized figures and movements who were deemed heterodox and suppressed. Alongside this focus on the diversity within Christianity itself, the ideal candidate should be prepared to engage the broader religious and social world of Late Antiquity addressing how Christian beliefs, practices, debates, and moral imaginaries took root in a culturally and ethnically heterogenous world. This might include, for example, addressing Jewish traditions, ancient Mediterranean traditions, classical Greco-Roman philosophies, and eventually the emergence of Islam.
The position involves undergraduate teaching in the University Core, the Theological Studies Major and Minor programs, as well as in the MA in Theology and MA in Pastoral Theology programs. The teaching load is defined as 2-2-2-3 over two years (i.e. two classes per regular semester and three classes every fourth semester). Desirable areas of scholarship and/or teaching may include: development and controversy within Christian doctrine (Christology, Trinity, Pneumatology, Anthropology, Eschatology); Patristics; the emergence of diverse Christian cultures in the form of institutions, literary and textual production (hagiography, monastic rules), or moral program; the history of Christian Asceticism, especially its diverse attitudes toward the body (i.e. food, sex, death, decay, and resurrection); the development of Christian ethics or political thought; the history of biblical interpretation (biblical scholarship, competing exegetical practices, ideal interpreters).
This is a tenure-track faculty appointment. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. or other relevant doctoral degree (e.g., Th.D) from an accredited institution. ABD candidates will be considered but must fulfill all degree requirements by August 15, 2027. This full-time, 9-month academic appointment (August – May) has an annual salary paid over 12 consecutive months, allowing for continuous benefits coverage. Visa sponsorship may be available for qualified candidates.

Please note that a maximum of 5 PDFs may be uploaded with each file size limited to 5MB. Only online applications will be accepted.
Applications missing any of the materials or arriving after September 8, 2026 will not be considered. Questions may be directed to: Amir Hussain, Late Antiquity Search Committee: amir.husain@lmu.edu. Preliminary interviews will be conducted virtually on Zoom in October, with short-listed candidates invited to campus for interviews in early November.

Please also include a sample of your scholarly work. Unofficial transcript from candidate’s doctoral program(s).

Who We Are
The Department of Political Science and International Relations at Loyola Marymount University (LMU), a Carnegie-classified R2 institution in the mainstream of American Catholic higher education, seeks outstanding applicants for the position of Assistant Professor (Tenure-Track) who value its Mission and share its commitment to inclusive excellence and the building of a just society. LMU is a Hispanic‑Serving Institution (HSI), Black‑Serving Institution (BSI), and Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander‑Serving Institution (AANAPISI), animating servingness for all persons, regardless of identity or beliefs, through its mission and Jesuit, Marymount educational traditions.
Appointment Type and Details
This is a tenure-track faculty appointment. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Political Science by the position start date of August 15, 2027. This full-time, 9-month academic appointment (August – May) has an annual salary paid over 12 consecutive months, allowing for continuous benefits coverage.
Position Responsibilities
The Department of Political Science and International Relations invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Latino politics (with a focus on the U.S. context). The successful candidate is also expected to teach a class on immigration politics.
Faculty responsibilities include maintaining an active program of scholarship, teaching and advising undergraduate students, and contributing to department and university service. Department tenure-track faculty members typically teach on a two-year 2-2-2-3 course rotation (that is, the teaching load is 2-2 one year and 2-3 the following year) within a 40% research, 40% teaching, and 20% service model.
Successful candidates will embrace the department’s mission of helping students become informed, analytically reflective, and engaged global citizens. The Department of Urban and Environmental Studies at Loyola Marymount University (LMU), a Carnegie-classified R2 institution in the mainstream of American Catholic higher education, seeks outstanding applicants for two tenure-line positions in urban studies who value its mission and share its commitment to inclusive excellence and the building of a just society. LMU is federally recognized as a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI) and is recognized by the State of California as a Black-Serving Institution (BSI). These designations reflect the university's continuing commitment to supporting student success, belonging, and thriving within a diverse academic community. As a Catholic, Jesuit, and Marymount university, LMU values faculty who engage students as whole persons and pursue scholarly work that promotes justice, equity, and the Common Good.

A teacher-scholar conducts research and creative work that contributes to the larger body of knowledge while setting an example for the importance of lifelong learning. Both positions are tenure-line faculty appointments. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in urban studies, planning, geography, or a closely related field by the position start date of August 2027. ABD applicants who anticipate completion of the doctorate by August 2027 will also be considered.

The Department of Urban and Environmental Studies invites applications from emerging and established scholars to fill two tenure-line positions in urban studies with expertise in urban planning or urban geography, beginning August 2027. One successful candidate will be appointed at the rank of Assistant Professor, and one will be hired at Assistant or Associate Professor based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated achievements. The rank determination will be made in accordance with university policies and standards.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Health Sciences & Risk Management
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Summary:
The Arkansas State University Department of Health Sciences & Risk Management invites applications for an Assistant Professor of Health Sciences & Risk Management (tenure-track) to begin in Fall 2027. The position is full-time (9-month) and tenure-track.
Duties & Responsibilities:
The primary teaching assignment and research focus will be in the Department’s Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management Program. The ideal candidate will demonstrate potential for an active, high impact emergency management research program. Responsibilities include producing peer-reviewed publications, presenting at professional conferences, and applying for external funding. Additional responsibilities include preparing, developing, and teaching undergraduate and graduate courses across multiple programs in the Department of Health Sciences and Risk Management. Applicants should have the ability to teach a broad range of courses across disciplines such as emergency management, health and/or public administration, policy, research methods, and program development and evaluation. Faculty are expected to maintain regular office hours, mentor undergraduate and graduate students, and participate in course/program assessment. Faculty are also expected to engage in departmental, college, university, and professional service activities that are in the best interest of the students, university, community, and the discipline at large. The ideal candidate will contribute to the development, assessment, and advancement of academic programs, including curriculum development, program assessment, workforce alignment, and engagement with external stakeholders.
Arkansas State University is a public research university located in Jonesboro, AR. Arkansas State University is designated by the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education as a “Research 2: High Research Spending and Doctorate Production” institution. The Department of Health Sciences & Risk Management has a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary focus across its programs in Disaster Preparedness & Emergency Management, Dietetics/Nutritional Science, Public Health, Occupational & Environmental Safety & Health, and Health Studies.
Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:
• Strong computer/technology skills required, or possess the ability to easily obtain needed skills. (Microsoft Office, Blackboard Learn and/or Canvas, variety of WEB based programs, etc.)
• Strong written and verbal communication skills required.
General Days/Hours:
Monday - Friday
8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.
Additional hours as requested and/or needed
Regular and reliable attendance
Application Instructions
Qualified applicants should submit their (1) curriculum vitae, (2) a statement of purpose indicating research interests and teaching philosophy, (3) a writing sample (recent peer-reviewed article or dissertation chapter), and (4) contact information for three academic references, that can speak to your research and teaching, that will be contacted if chosen for an interview. All materials should be submitted online via Taleo, and all items must be submitted to be considered. Application review will begin on the closing date in Taleo and will continue until the position is filled.
Questions can be directed to the search committee chair, Dr. Amy Hyman, at ahyman@astate.edu.
Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications include a Ph.D. or terminal research degree in an emergency management or closely related discipline. Candidates who are ABD will also be considered, provided they obtain their degree by July 1, 2027.
Candidates should have a strong research agenda in the emergency management discipline, or a closely related discipline with an emergency management focus, with evidence of peer-reviewed publications and/or external funding, or the potential to quickly develop a strong research agenda and be immediately successful regarding research and in obtaining external funding. Candidates should also have experience with face-to-face and online teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels.

jobs.title: Art & Design: Assistant Professor in Graphic Design -- JR10014575
jobs.description:
Job Details
POSITION: The Department of Art & Design seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor candidate with experience in graphic design, teaching, and making, whose practice bridges analog and digital processes. Candidates who can demonstrate experience in typography, web development, UI/UX, and/or community-based design practices will be preferred. The department values candidates who are proactive regarding emerging tools and technologies relevant to contemporary graphic design practice. This appointment carries an initial two-year probationary appointment beginning with the 2027/2028 academic year.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Terminal Degree (e.g. MFA) in Graphic Design or a related field (completed prior to start date Fall ‘27) - Evidence of productive scholarly activity and/or professional design practice. Proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud applications. Demonstrable ability to teach required and elective studio courses at all undergraduate levels to majors and non-majors.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Two or more years of university-level teaching experience. Ability to revise, enhance, and/or expand the design curriculum through expertise in any of the following; UI/UX, community-based design, critical design theory, branding identity, motion graphics, 3D-Modeling, animation, digital fabrication, experimental typography, and emerging technologies. Experience in collaborative design processes. Commitment to teaching foundations level courses. Willingness to engage in community-based projects and/or project-based research that connects academia and practice. Commitment to inclusive pedagogy, accessibility, and ethical practice, including responsible integration of emerging technologies (e.g. AI). Ability to collaborate with other professional/academic disciplines, engaging with diverse student populations.
DUTIES: Core responsibilities include teaching 3 courses (or the equivalent of 12 contact hours) per semester at all levels (Foundations to Capstone); participating in research and creative or scholarly activities; providing academic advising to students as assigned (including internships); engage in service to the department, university, and profession. We seek individuals who can meaningfully mentor and serve the needs of all students
DEPARTMENT: The Department of Art & Design consists of twelve faculty and staff. The department serves over 200 students through its majors and minor programs and also participates in General Education offerings. It offers the following programs: Bachelor of Fine Arts – Integrated Visual Arts, BA/BS in Studio Art and Graphic Communications, and Liberal Arts BA/BS in Studio Art. The department offers minors in studio art and art history. Design courses are also part of the Multimedia Communication minor. The Department houses the Ruth Foster Art Gallery, maintains a woodshop, a finishing lab, and a fabrication lab. For more information regarding the Department of Art & Design, please visit the following website: https://www.uwec.edu/academics/college-arts-sciences/departments-programs/art-design/
UNIVERSITY and EAU CLAIRE COMMUNITY: UW-Eau Claire, an institution of approximately 9,000 students and 1,100 faculty and staff, is consistently recognized as a top comprehensive university in the Midwest and is widely known as a leader in faculty-undergraduate research and study abroad. We strive for excellence in liberal education and select graduate and professional programs through commitment to teaching and learning and dedication to our core values of diversity, sustainability, leadership, and innovation.
The City of Eau Claire, situated at the confluence of the Chippewa and Eau Claire rivers, is at the center of a metropolitan area of approximately 100,000 people located 90 miles east of Minneapolis/St. Paul. The area features beautiful parks and trails, strong public schools and health care facilities, a vibrant arts scene and local food culture, and abundant indoor and outdoor recreational opportunities.

The university reserves the right to contact additional references with notice given to the candidates at an appropriate time in the process. Employment will require a background check.
